objective: ExtractionProvider contract suite across the fake, CLI and Anthropic adapters, the log part of the secrets scan (NFR6, RS-29), the HTTP contract scenarios for the phase D routes (FU-13, FU-18), and the degraded-extraction browser journey with the 360 px table check (RS-03, FU-17).
context: Built against spec.md (Testing Strategy, Observability, AI design) and the d1-d4 handoffs. Nothing here calls a model: the fake is simulated, the CLI adapter runs against the stub claude binary replaying the recorded-shape transcript (not a capture of the real CLI), the Anthropic adapter against a loopback stub. The results prove the adapters' mapping, the pipeline and the harness, not model quality. test/scan/secrets.test.js did not exist, so the log part is a new file (the plan's 'keep the existing scan content' had nothing to keep). The request-view fixtures request-view-planned/infeasible/reserved are d4's and lack the additive capabilities key, so those three rows carry optional: ['capabilities'] (I do not own the fixtures). GET /api/requests/:id/image returns bytes, not JSON, so it has a table row with binary: true that checks status, detected type, nosniff, CSP sandbox, no-store and the exact bytes. The fake provider has no busy fault (FAKE_FAULTS has four names), so the PROVIDER_BUSY row of the shared suite is SKIPPED for the fake and reported as skipped.
expectedOutput: The four test deliverables plus their helpers, with npm test and npm run test:browser green and the phase E contract rows still skipped under FU-18.

Guard note: the Bash guard refused a harmless sed command whose script was '178d' (read as a path outside the task's ownership) and a heredoc containing backticks (read as a substitution in an eccode command). Both were redone with the Edit tool; nothing was written outside the ownership.

The cli x PROVIDER_TIMEOUT case uses a 300 ms adapter timeout against a stub that never answers, and the anthropic one 150 ms against a 3 s delayed reply: the outcome does not depend on timing (the stub never answers in time) but they do wait for the timeout, about 0.5 s together.

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson is about a hook or guard choosing a project root for a write target. This task writes tests, builds no hook, guard or root discovery, and every write was accepted by the guard in the nested record, so none of its 'Applies when' conditions hold.
